key_insight: Shield synthesis is reframed from a runtime safety controller into a design-time analysis tool that certifies whether a network topology and specification are defensible.
engineering_relevance: For network defense, this provides a formal way to compare architectures, identify winning regions, and quantify how robust a topology is under adversarial play.
method: Compile defender and attacker temporal-logic specs into automata.
Build a constrained two-player safety game and compute attractors/winning regions.
Extract a defensibility verdict plus topology-level metrics and a shield-derived fingerprint.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a what-if analysis showing that small architectural changes can strongly affect operational outcomes even when formal safety margins stay nearly unchanged.
watch_item: The framework depends on accurate specification modeling and game construction, so mismatches between the formal model and real network behavior could weaken the verdict.
paper_title: Beyond Runtime Enforcement: Shield Synthesis as Defensibility Analysis for Adversarial Networks
